correctness.rationale: Exact finite-game type recurrence reduces rank-three vertex-transitive graph equivalence to equality of pair extension-signature sets. Circular intervals yield an exact common-ball count t(d)=(2k+1-d)_+ +(d-(n-2k-1))_+. Endpoint-subtracted quantities c, u, w determine all four adjacency choices for a third vertex. Exhaustive symbolic sign ranges for every integer n>=2k+1,k>=1 give eleven pairwise distinct signatures, and minimization of admissible n proves the sharp eleven-vertex bound. A separate direct graph oracle reproduces all 55 representative comparisons; finite tests are only corroboration. No infinite fact is inferred from finite computations.

originality.rationale: The first-order three-round type classification of cycle powers with k>=2, including all parameter cross-collisions and the sharp representative bound, is not a corollary of Brown–Hoshino’s ordinary-cycle theorem or Lin et al.’s cycle-power recognition characterization. Actual full-text primary source inspections and multiple semantic claim/equivalence searches were conducted. Older results on rooted counting colour refinement have different quantification and do not dominate the unpointed FO statement. Residual unindexed-coverage risk remains.
residual_risks: A theorem with equivalent implications may exist in unindexed specialist literature even though exact claim/alias searches found none.
The present theorem only handles quantifier rank at most three, in pure adjacency, and is sharp within the cycle-power family; stronger signatures or all finite graphs are not classified.

value.rationale: This is a complete and sharp first-order rank-three invariant for the natural infinite two-parameter family of cycle powers, including cross-exponent collisions and six nonordinary-power regimes. It yields an optimal eleven-vertex canonical testing family for every rank-three sentence and explains the exact logical visibility of the circular adjacency radius, a specific mathematical classification beyond isolated computations.
